security_audit.summary: The backticks are Markdown, and the secret reference documents authentication without asking the assistant to read or expose the key. The intended remote calls send inputs to OpenAny. Paid calls require approval, but the skill does not require showing the user the price, data to be sent, or known side effects before approval.

remediation.issue: The paid-call approval step does not define what the user must review.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact API version, destination, quoted price, data to be sent, and known side effects. Ask again if any of these details change.

remediation.issue: Search queries and execution inputs leave the local client.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose what the gateway receives and when providers may receive it. Use only the necessary data and keep authentication in the client.

content.user_title: Find and Run APIs and AI Models with OpenAny
content.value_statement: Finding a suitable API or AI model often means checking several catalogs. OpenAny lets you browse one catalog, review public prices, and approve calls individually.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve catalog counts for data APIs by category and AI models by modality.
Search for APIs and AI models using a business query or a returned filter.
Look up an entry's input schema, API version, and published price.
Use the published version and input schema to execute an authenticated call after user approval.
Report the result or gateway error returned by a call.
limitations: The skill needs the OpenAny MCP server connection and does not use the full catalog's tool names.
Execution requires an OpenAny API key and may spend your balance or cause side effects.
The skill does not declare a fixed price or verify the final charge from an HTTP success response.
Search queries and execution inputs are sent to the remote OpenAny service.

use_cases.title: Research Data Sources
use_cases.description: Browse company and finance API categories and find entries relevant to a research task without making a paid call.

use_cases.title: Review API Requirements
use_cases.description: Check the input schema, version, and public price of an API before deciding whether to integrate it.

use_cases.title: Compare Model Options
use_cases.description: Find models for a content task and compare their documented inputs and prices before approving a trial.

prompt_templates.title: Browse the Catalog
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the available data API categories and AI model modalities. Use the counts from OpenAny. Do not run a paid call.

prompt_templates.title: Search for a Data API
prompt_templates.prompt: Find OpenAny APIs for public company profiles. Summarize what the results offer. Do not run a paid call.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Find two available text models for summarization, if possible. Compare their API versions, required inputs, and published prices. Do not run either model.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare One Approved Call
prompt_templates.prompt: Find an API for public company profiles and prepare a request using only a public company name. Show the API version, destination, published price, inputs, and known side effects. Wait for my approval before running it. Do not retry if execution or charging is unclear.

output_examples.input: Find data APIs that offer public company profiles. Do not run a paid call.
output_examples.output: I found a company profile option and a company search option. The profile option fits when you already know the company name. No paid call was made.

output_examples.input: Report the result of my approved request.
output_examples.output: The gateway returned a timeout. I cannot confirm whether the request ran or incurred a charge. I did not retry it.

best_practices: Use the catalog results for names and counts, and check the entry details for the current published price.
Before approving a paid call, review the destination, price, exact input, and known side effects.
Keep the API key in your client's supported secret configuration and send only the data needed for the task.
anti_patterns: Pasting the API key into chat or including it in request data.
Treating a successful tool listing or HTTP response as proof that a paid call completed or was charged.
Retrying a call when you cannot confirm whether it ran or incurred a charge.

faq.question: Do I need an API key to browse?
faq.answer: No. The connected OpenAny server supports browsing, search, and published pricing without a key.

faq.question: When is an API key required?
faq.answer: An OpenAny API key is required to execute a call. Configure it through your MCP client's supported secret settings.

faq.question: Can I see a price before running a call?
faq.answer: Yes. Look up the entry to see its published price before deciding whether to approve the call.

faq.question: Will a search run a paid API call?
faq.answer: No. Search finds catalog entries. Running an API or model is a separate step that requires your approval.

faq.question: Where do search queries and execution inputs go?
faq.answer: They go to the remote OpenAny MCP service. Use only information you can share with that service.

faq.question: What should I do if a paid call times out?
faq.answer: Review the gateway error. Do not retry until you know whether the call ran and whether it incurred a charge.
